reference.title: Lever Belt Romanian Deadlift
reference.listing: Video (title from the listing URL; the page could not be fetched from this environment, so the movement follows the exercise name and standard coaching)
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

breathing.pattern: Breathe in and brace at the top, lower with the brace, breathe out as you stand.
breathing.cadence: About 2.2 s down, short pause, about 1.3 s up

prescription.load: Machine load is user-chosen: pick a weight you can move through the full range shown with good form, leaving about 2-3 reps in reserve (RPE 7-8).

cues.text: Hip belt snug and hooked to the lever, feet hip width, knees soft; hold the handles in front for balance.
Push the hips back against the belt, keep the back flat and let the chest tip forward.
Stop where the hamstrings are stretched with the back still flat.
Drive the hips forward through the belt to stand tall.
Stand tall without leaning back; breathe and repeat.

mistakes.mistake: Rounding the back to go lower
mistakes.fix: Stop where the back is still flat; the range comes from the hips.

mistakes.mistake: Squatting the weight down (knees bending a lot)
mistakes.fix: Keep the knee bend small and constant; push the hips back.

kinematics.norm: Peak hip flexion about 98-103 degrees in barbell and landmine RDLs (McCurdy 2025)
Small, nearly constant soft knee bend, about 15-25 degrees (clinical opinion)
Neutral spine; about 7 degrees of lumbar motion was measured in RDLs (McCurdy 2025)

kinematics.peak: 2.2 s down to a handle height of 37 cm (upper shin), 0.3 s pause, 1.3 s up, 1.4 s reset
kinematics.norm: Controlled, about 2 s down and 1-1.5 s up (clinical opinion)

kinematics.setup: Belt ring 17 cm ahead of the hips (pelvis frame); lever pivot 35 cm ahead of and 88 cm below the ring
kinematics.peak: Lever swings 22.3°; ring within 0.02 cm of the lever end
kinematics.norm: The load hangs from the hips through the belt, so the spine and shoulders carry none of it (machine design; common coaching)

sources.title: GymVisual, Lever Belt Romanian Deadlift, video (movement reference)
McCurdy & Koldenhoven 2025, comparison of muscle activation and range of motion between the traditional and landmine Romanian deadlift (Int J Strength Cond 5(1))
Lee et al. 2018, an electromyographic and kinetic comparison of conventional and Romanian deadlifts (J Exerc Sci Fit; PMC6323186)

cautions: Fit the belt low on the hips and check the hook and chain before loading the lever.
Hold the handles lightly for balance; the legs and hips do the work.
Stop if sharp pain, numbness, tingling or giving-way occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Low-back pain: shorten the range and keep the spine neutral; seek advice if pain persists.
modify: Tight hamstrings: stop higher (around the knees) and bend the knees a little more.
Balance: stand with the feet a little wider.
regressions: Bodyweight hip hinge with a dowel on the back.

muscleNotes.hamstrings_r: Lengthen under load as the hips hinge back, then extend the hips. Biceps femoris averaged about 41% MVIC lowering and 72% MVIC rising in a barbell RDL (McCurdy 2025).
muscleNotes.hamstrings_l: Lengthen under load as the hips hinge back, then extend the hips. Biceps femoris averaged about 41% MVIC lowering and 72% MVIC rising in a barbell RDL (McCurdy 2025).
muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Extends the hips on the way up; gluteus maximus activity was a little lower in the Romanian than the conventional deadlift (Lee 2018).
muscleNotes.glute_max_l: Extends the hips on the way up; gluteus maximus activity was a little lower in the Romanian than the conventional deadlift (Lee 2018).
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_r: Hold the spine neutral; lumbar motion stayed about 7 degrees in the RDLs measured by McCurdy 2025.
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_l: Hold the spine neutral; lumbar motion stayed about 7 degrees in the RDLs measured by McCurdy 2025.
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_r: Hold the handles for balance (light grip).
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_l: Hold the handles for balance (light grip).
muscleNotes.lats_r: Keep the dumbbells close to the legs.
muscleNotes.lats_l: Keep the dumbbells close to the legs.
muscleNotes.upper_traps_r: Hold the shoulders against the pull of the dumbbells.
